OpenThreadToken@WIN32API.INC.desc: Opens the access token associated with a thread. Returns nonzero on success and the token handle in the last parameter.

GetTokenInformation@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves a specified type of information (user, groups, privileges, etc.) about an access token into a caller buffer. Returns nonzero on success.

SetTokenInformation@WIN32API.INC.desc: Sets various types of information for a specified access token, such as owner, primary group or default DACL. Returns nonzero on success.

AdjustTokenPrivileges_WIN32API@WIN32API..desc: Enables or disables privileges in the specified access token; requires TOKEN_ADJUST_PRIVILEGES access. Returns nonzero on success; check GetLastError for ERROR_NOT_ALL_ASSIGNED.

AdjustTokenGroups@WIN32API.INC.desc: Enables or disables groups already present in the specified access token. Returns nonzero on success.

PrivilegeCheck@WIN32API.INC.desc: Determines whether a specified set of privileges is enabled in an access token; the result is returned in the last parameter.

AccessCheckAndAuditAlarm@WIN32API.INC.desc: Determines whether a security descriptor grants access to the client being impersonated by the calling thread, and generates audit messages if needed.

ObjectOpenAuditAlarm@WIN32API.INC.desc: Generates audit messages when a client application attempts to gain access to an object or to create a new one. WIN32API.INC declared it from kernel32; the build uses advapi32.

ObjectPrivilegeAuditAlarm@WIN32API.INC.desc: Generates an audit message in the security event log when privileged operations are performed on an object.

ObjectCloseAuditAlarm@WIN32API.INC.desc: Generates an audit message in the security event log when a handle to a private object is deleted.

PrivilegedServiceAuditAlarm@WIN32API.INC.desc: Generates an audit message in the security event log when a privileged system service operation is attempted.

IsValidSid@WIN32API.INC.desc: Validates a security identifier (SID) by checking its revision and subauthority count. Returns nonzero if the SID is valid.

EqualSid@WIN32API.INC.desc: Tests two security identifiers (SIDs) for equality. Returns nonzero if they are equal.

EqualPrefixSid@WIN32API.INC.desc: Tests two SID prefix values for equality (all subauthorities except the last). Returns nonzero if equal.

GetSidLengthRequired@WIN32API.INC.desc: Returns the length in bytes of the buffer required to store a SID with the specified number of subauthorities.

AllocateAndInitializeSid@WIN32API.INC.desc: Allocates and initializes a SID with up to eight subauthorities. The SID must be freed with FreeSid.

FreeSid@WIN32API.INC.desc: Frees a SID previously allocated with AllocateAndInitializeSid.

InitializeSid@WIN32API.INC.desc: Initializes a caller-allocated SID structure with an identifier authority and number of subauthorities.

GetSidIdentifierAuthority@WIN32API.INC.desc: Returns a pointer to the SID_IDENTIFIER_AUTHORITY structure in a specified SID.

GetSidSubAuthority@WIN32API.INC.desc: Returns a pointer to a specified subauthority in a SID.

GetSidSubAuthorityCount@WIN32API.INC.desc: Returns a pointer to the member of a SID that holds the subauthority count.

GetLengthSid@WIN32API.INC.desc: Returns the length in bytes of a valid security identifier (SID).

CopySid@WIN32API.INC.desc: Copies a security identifier (SID) to a buffer. Returns nonzero on success.

AreAllAccessesGranted@WIN32API.INC.desc: Checks whether a set of requested access rights has been granted; returns nonzero if all requested rights are in the granted mask.

AreAnyAccessesGranted@WIN32API.INC.desc: Tests whether any of a set of requested access rights has been granted; returns nonzero if at least one is granted.

MapGenericMask@WIN32API.INC.desc: Maps the generic access rights in an access mask to specific and standard rights using a GENERIC_MAPPING structure.

IsValidAcl@WIN32API.INC.desc: Validates an access control list (ACL). Returns nonzero if the ACL is valid.

InitializeAcl@WIN32API.INC.desc: Initializes a new, empty ACL structure in a caller buffer. Returns nonzero on success.

GetAclInformation@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves information about an access control list, such as revision or size and ACE count.

SetAclInformation@WIN32API.INC.desc: Sets information about an access control list (ACL), such as its revision.

AddAce@WIN32API.INC.desc: Adds one or more access control entries (ACEs) to a specified ACL at a given index.

DeleteAce@WIN32API.INC.desc: Deletes the access control entry at the specified index from an ACL.

GetAce@WIN32API.INC.desc: Obtains a pointer to the access control entry at the specified index in an ACL.

AddAccessAllowedAce@WIN32API.INC.desc: Adds an access-allowed ACE for a specified SID and access mask to the end of an ACL.

AddAccessDeniedAce@WIN32API.INC.desc: Adds an access-denied ACE for a specified SID and access mask to the end of an ACL.

AddAuditAccessAce@WIN32API.INC.desc: Adds a system-audit ACE to a system ACL (SACL) for a SID, auditing successful and/or failed access.

FindFirstFreeAce@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves a pointer to the first free byte in an access control list (ACL).

InitializeSecurityDescriptor@WIN32API.IN.desc: Initializes a new security descriptor in absolute format with no SACL, DACL, owner or group.

IsValidSecurityDescriptor@WIN32API.INC.desc: Determines whether the components of a security descriptor are valid. Returns nonzero if valid.

GetSecurityDescriptorLength@WIN32API.INC.desc: Returns the length in bytes of a structurally valid security descriptor, including associated structures.

GetSecurityDescriptorControl@WIN32API.IN.desc: Retrieves the control information and revision of a security descriptor.

SetSecurityDescriptorDacl@WIN32API.INC.desc: Sets information in a discretionary access control list (DACL) of a security descriptor; a NULL DACL grants full access to everyone.

GetSecurityDescriptorDacl@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves a pointer to the discretionary access control list (DACL) in a security descriptor and whether it is present/defaulted.

SetSecurityDescriptorSacl@WIN32API.INC.desc: Sets information in a system access control list (SACL) of a security descriptor.

GetSecurityDescriptorSacl@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves a pointer to the system access control list (SACL) in a security descriptor.

SetSecurityDescriptorOwner@WIN32API.INC.desc: Sets the owner information of an absolute-format security descriptor.

GetSecurityDescriptorOwner@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves the owner SID from a security descriptor.

SetSecurityDescriptorGroup@WIN32API.INC.desc: Sets the primary group information of an absolute-format security descriptor.

GetSecurityDescriptorGroup@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves the primary group SID from a security descriptor.

CreatePrivateObjectSecurity@WIN32API.INC.desc: Allocates and initializes a self-relative security descriptor for a new private object created by a resource manager.

SetPrivateObjectSecurity@WIN32API.INC.desc: Modifies the security descriptor of a private object maintained by a resource manager.

GetPrivateObjectSecurity@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves information from the security descriptor of a private object.

DestroyPrivateObjectSecurity@WIN32API.IN.desc: Deletes the security descriptor of a private object created by CreatePrivateObjectSecurity.

MakeSelfRelativeSD@WIN32API.INC.desc: Creates a self-relative security descriptor from one in absolute format.

MakeAbsoluteSD@WIN32API.INC.desc: Creates an absolute-format security descriptor from one in self-relative format.

SetFileSecurity@WIN32API.INC.desc: Sets the security of a file or directory object. Returns nonzero on success. Superseded by SetNamedSecurityInfo.

GetFileSecurity@WIN32API.INC.desc: Obtains specified information about the security of a file or directory into a security descriptor buffer.

SetKernelObjectSecurity@WIN32API.INC.desc: Sets the security of a kernel object, such as a process, thread or event, given its handle.

FindFirstChangeNotification@WIN32API.INC.desc: Creates a change notification handle that is signaled when a specified change occurs in a directory (optionally its subtree).

FindNextChangeNotification@WIN32API.INC.desc: Requests that the system signal a change notification handle the next time it detects an appropriate change.

FindCloseChangeNotification@WIN32API.INC.desc: Stops change notification handle monitoring and closes the handle.

VirtualLock@WIN32API.INC.desc: Locks the specified region of the process's virtual address space into physical memory so it is not paged out.

VirtualUnlock@WIN32API.INC.desc: Unlocks a range of pages in the virtual address space of a process so the system can page them out.

MapViewOfFileEx@WIN32API.INC.desc: Maps a view of a file mapping into the address space of the calling process, optionally at a suggested base address. Returns the starting address.

FatalExit@WIN32API.INC.desc: Transfers execution control to the debugger; intended for debugging only. The process terminates if no debugger is present.

RaiseException@WIN32API.INC.desc: Raises an exception in the calling thread with the specified code, flags and arguments.

UnhandledExceptionFilter@WIN32API.INC.desc: Passes unhandled exceptions to the debugger if the process is being debugged; otherwise may show an Application Error dialog.

CreateThread@WIN32API.INC.desc: Creates a thread to execute within the virtual address space of the calling process. Returns a thread handle, or NULL on failure.

CreateRemoteThread@WIN32API.INC.desc: Creates a thread that runs in the virtual address space of another process. Returns a thread handle, or NULL on failure.

SetThreadPriority@WIN32API.INC.desc: Sets the priority value for the specified thread relative to its process priority class. Returns nonzero on success.

GetThreadPriority@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves the priority value for the specified thread, or THREAD_PRIORITY_ERROR_RETURN on failure.

GetThreadTimes@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves creation, exit, kernel and user time information for the specified thread as FILETIME values.

ExitThread@WIN32API.INC.desc: Ends the calling thread with the specified exit code.

TerminateThread@WIN32API.INC.desc: Forcibly terminates a thread. Dangerous: the thread gets no chance to clean up; use only in extreme cases.

GetExitCodeThread@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves the termination status of the specified thread; STILL_ACTIVE (259) if it is still running.

GetThreadSelectorEntry@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves a descriptor table entry for the specified selector and thread (x86 only, used by debuggers).

GetCommTimeouts@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves the time-out parameters for all read and write operations on a communications device into a COMMTIMEOUTS structure.

BuildCommDCB@WIN32API.INC.desc: Fills a DCB structure with values from a device-control string such as "baud=9600 parity=N data=8 stop=1".

BuildCommDCBAndTimeouts@WIN32API.INC.desc: Translates a device-definition string into DCB codes and optionally sets COMMTIMEOUTS values.

TransmitCommChar@WIN32API.INC.desc: Transmits a specified character ahead of any pending data in the output buffer of a communications device.

SetCommBreak@WIN32API.INC.desc: Suspends character transmission and places the communications line in a break state until ClearCommBreak is called.

SetCommMask@WIN32API.INC.desc: Specifies the set of events (EV_RXCHAR, EV_CTS, etc.) to be monitored for a communications device.

ClearCommBreak@WIN32API.INC.desc: Restores character transmission on a communications device and places the line in a nonbreak state.

EscapeCommFunction@WIN32API.INC.desc: Directs a communications device to perform an extended function, such as setting or clearing DTR or RTS.

GetCommMask@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves the value of the event mask for a communications device.

GetCommProperties@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves information about the properties of a communications device into a COMMPROP structure.

GetCommModemStatus@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves the modem control-register values (CTS, DSR, RING, RLSD) of a communications device.

WaitCommEvent@WIN32API.INC.desc: Waits for an event to occur for a communications device; the events are set with SetCommMask.

SetTapePosition@WIN32API.INC.desc: Sets the tape position on the specified tape device.

GetTapePosition@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves the current address of the tape, in logical or absolute blocks.

PrepareTape@WIN32API.INC.desc: Prepares the tape to be accessed or removed (load, unload, lock, tension, etc.).

EraseTape@WIN32API.INC.desc: Erases all or part of a tape.

CreateTapePartition@WIN32API.INC.desc: Reformats a tape and creates partitions on it.

WriteTapemark@WIN32API.INC.desc: Writes a specified number of filemarks, setmarks or other tapemarks to a tape device.

GetTapeStatus@WIN32API.INC.desc: Determines whether the tape device is ready to process tape commands; returns NO_ERROR if ready.

GetTapeParameters@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves information that describes the tape or the tape drive.

SetTapeParameters@WIN32API.INC.desc: Specifies the block size of a tape or configuration information for a tape drive.

Beep@WIN32API.INC.desc: Generates simple tones on the speaker with the specified frequency (Hz) and duration (ms). Synchronous; returns nonzero on success.

MulDiv@WIN32API.INC.desc: Multiplies two 32-bit values and divides the 64-bit result by a third value, returning the rounded result, or -1 on overflow or division by zero.

GetSystemTime@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves the current system date and time in UTC into a SYSTEMTIME structure.

SetSystemTime@WIN32API.INC.desc: Sets the current system date and time in UTC; requires the SE_SYSTEMTIME_NAME privilege.

GetLocalTime@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves the current local date and time into a SYSTEMTIME structure.

SetLocalTime@WIN32API.INC.desc: Sets the current local date and time; requires the SE_SYSTEMTIME_NAME privilege.

GetSystemInfo@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves information about the current system (processor architecture, page size, number of processors) into a SYSTEM_INFO structure.

GetTimeZoneInformation@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves the current time zone settings; returns TIME_ZONE_ID_STANDARD, TIME_ZONE_ID_DAYLIGHT or TIME_ZONE_ID_UNKNOWN.

SetTimeZoneInformation@WIN32API.INC.desc: Sets the current time zone settings for the local computer; requires the SE_TIME_ZONE_NAME privilege.

SystemTimeToFileTime@WIN32API.INC.desc: Converts a SYSTEMTIME structure to file time format (100-ns intervals since 1601).

FileTimeToLocalFileTime@WIN32API.INC.desc: Converts a UTC file time to a local file time.

LocalFileTimeToFileTime@WIN32API.INC.desc: Converts a local file time to a UTC file time.

FileTimeToSystemTime@WIN32API.INC.desc: Converts a file time to SYSTEMTIME format.

CompareFileTime@WIN32API.INC.desc: Compares two file times; returns -1, 0 or 1 if the first is earlier, equal or later.

FileTimeToDosDateTime@WIN32API.INC.desc: Converts a file time to MS-DOS date and time values.

DosDateTimeToFileTime@WIN32API.INC.desc: Converts MS-DOS date and time values to a file time.

FormatMessage_WIN32API@WIN32API.INC.desc: Formats a message string from a message table, system error code or format string. Returns the number of characters stored, or 0 on failure.

CreatePipe@WIN32API.INC.desc: Creates an anonymous pipe and returns handles to its read and write ends. Returns nonzero on success.

ConnectNamedPipe@WIN32API.INC.desc: Enables a named pipe server process to wait for a client process to connect to an instance of a named pipe.

DisconnectNamedPipe@WIN32API.INC.desc: Disconnects the server end of a named pipe instance from a client process.

SetNamedPipeHandleState@WIN32API.INC.desc: Sets the read mode and blocking mode of the specified named pipe, and collection parameters for remote clients.

GetNamedPipeInfo@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves information about the specified named pipe (type, buffer sizes, maximum instances).

PeekNamedPipe@WIN32API.INC.desc: Copies data from a named or anonymous pipe into a buffer without removing it, and reports bytes available.

TransactNamedPipe@WIN32API.INC.desc: Combines writing a message to and reading a message from a named pipe into a single operation.

CreateMailslot@WIN32API.INC.desc: Creates a mailslot with the specified name and returns a handle a mailslot server can use. Returns INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE on failure.

GetMailslotInfo@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves information about the specified mailslot, such as next message size and message count.

SetMailslotInfo@WIN32API.INC.desc: Sets the time-out value used by the specified mailslot for a read operation.

MapViewOfFile@WIN32API.INC.desc: Maps a view of a file mapping into the address space of the calling process. Returns the starting address, or NULL on failure.

FlushViewOfFile@WIN32API.INC.desc: Writes to disk a byte range within a mapped view of a file.

UnmapViewOfFile@WIN32API.INC.desc: Unmaps a mapped view of a file from the calling process's address space.

lstrcmp@WIN32API.INC.desc: Compares two character strings, case-sensitive, using the user locale. Returns negative, zero or positive.

lstrcmpi@WIN32API.INC.desc: Compares two character strings, case-insensitive, using the user locale. Returns negative, zero or positive.

lstrlen@WIN32API.INC.desc: Determines the length of the specified string, not including the terminating null character.

lopen@WIN32API.INC.desc: Opens an existing file and returns a file handle. Obsolete, for 16-bit compatibility; use CreateFile instead.

lclose@WIN32API.INC.desc: Closes the specified file. Obsolete, for 16-bit compatibility; use CloseHandle instead.

lcreat@WIN32API.INC.desc: Creates or opens the specified file. Obsolete, for 16-bit compatibility; use CreateFile instead.

llseek@WIN32API.INC.desc: Repositions the file pointer of an open file. Obsolete, for 16-bit compatibility; use SetFilePointer instead.

lread@WIN32API.INC.desc: Reads data from the specified file. Obsolete, for 16-bit compatibility; use ReadFile instead.

lwrite@WIN32API.INC.desc: Writes data to the specified file. Obsolete, for 16-bit compatibility; use WriteFile instead.

hread@WIN32API.INC.desc: Reads data from the specified file. Obsolete, for 16-bit compatibility; use ReadFile instead.

hwrite@WIN32API.INC.desc: Writes data to the specified file. Obsolete, for 16-bit compatibility; use WriteFile instead.

TlsAlloc@WIN32API.INC.desc: Allocates a thread local storage (TLS) index. Returns the index, or TLS_OUT_OF_INDEXES on failure.

TlsGetValue@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves the value in the calling thread's thread local storage slot for the specified TLS index.

TlsSetValue@WIN32API.INC.desc: Stores a value in the calling thread's thread local storage slot for the specified TLS index.

TlsFree@WIN32API.INC.desc: Releases a thread local storage (TLS) index, making it available for reuse.

SleepEx@WIN32API.INC.desc: Suspends the current thread for the given milliseconds, or until an I/O completion callback or APC runs if alertable is TRUE.

WaitForSingleObjectEx@WIN32API.INC.desc: Waits until the object is signaled, an I/O completion routine or APC is queued (if alertable), or the time-out elapses.

WaitForMultipleObjectsEx@WIN32API.INC.desc: Waits until one or all of the objects are signaled, an APC or I/O completion routine runs (if alertable), or the time-out elapses.

BackupRead@WIN32API.INC.desc: Backs up a file or directory, including its security information, by reading data in a stream format.

BackupSeek@WIN32API.INC.desc: Seeks forward in a data stream initially accessed with BackupRead or BackupWrite.

BackupWrite@WIN32API.INC.desc: Restores a file or directory that was backed up using BackupRead.

CreateMutex@WIN32API.INC.desc: Creates or opens a named or unnamed mutex object. Returns a handle, or NULL on failure; ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS if the name existed.

OpenMutex@WIN32API.INC.desc: Opens an existing named mutex object. Returns a handle, or NULL on failure.

CreateEvent@WIN32API.INC.desc: Creates or opens a named or unnamed event object (manual- or auto-reset, initial state). Returns a handle, or NULL on failure.

OpenEvent@WIN32API.INC.desc: Opens an existing named event object. Returns a handle, or NULL on failure.

CreateSemaphore@WIN32API.INC.desc: Creates or opens a named or unnamed semaphore object with initial and maximum counts. Returns a handle, or NULL on failure.

OpenSemaphore@WIN32API.INC.desc: Opens an existing named semaphore object. Returns a handle, or NULL on failure.

CreateFileMapping@WIN32API.INC.desc: Creates or opens a named or unnamed file mapping object for a file or the paging file. Returns a handle, or NULL on failure.

OpenFileMapping@WIN32API.INC.desc: Opens a named file mapping object. Returns a handle, or NULL on failure.

GetLogicalDriveStrings@WIN32API.INC.desc: Fills a buffer with null-separated strings naming the valid drives (e.g. C:\). Returns the length of the string copied.

IsBadReadPtr@WIN32API.INC.desc: Verifies that the calling process has read access to a memory range. Obsolete and should not be used.

IsBadWritePtr@WIN32API.INC.desc: Verifies that the calling process has write access to a memory range. Obsolete and should not be used.

IsBadStringPtr@WIN32API.INC.desc: Verifies that the calling process has read access to a string, up to a maximum length. Obsolete and should not be used.

IsBadHugeReadPtr@WIN32API.INC.desc: Verifies read access to a memory range. Obsolete, for 16-bit compatibility; same as IsBadReadPtr in Win32 and should not be used.

IsBadHugeWritePtr@WIN32API.INC.desc: Verifies write access to a memory range. Obsolete, for 16-bit compatibility; same as IsBadWritePtr in Win32 and should not be used.

LookupAccountSid@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves the account name and domain name for a SID, plus the SID type.

LookupAccountName@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves the SID and domain name for a specified account name on a system.

LookupPrivilegeValue_WIN32API@WIN32API.I.desc: Retrieves the locally unique identifier (LUID) that represents a privilege name (e.g. SeShutdownPrivilege) on a system.

LookupPrivilegeName@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves the privilege name corresponding to a locally unique identifier (LUID).

LookupPrivilegeDisplayName@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves the human-readable display name for a specified privilege.

AllocateLocallyUniqueId@WIN32API.INC.desc: Allocates a locally unique identifier (LUID), unique until the system restarts.

GetComputerName_WIN32API@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves the NetBIOS name of the local computer into a buffer; the size parameter receives the length.

SetComputerName@WIN32API.INC.desc: Sets a new NetBIOS name for the local computer; takes effect after restart.

GetUserName_WIN32API@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves the name of the user associated with the current thread into a buffer.

QueryPerformanceCounter_WIN32API@WIN32AP.desc: Retrieves the current value of the high-resolution performance counter as a 64-bit count.

QueryPerformanceFrequency_WIN32API@WIN32.desc: Retrieves the frequency of the performance counter in counts per second (fixed at boot).

IsValidCodePage@WIN32API.INC.desc: Determines whether a specified code page is valid (installed). Returns nonzero if valid.

GetACP@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves the current Windows ANSI code page identifier for the operating system.

GetCPInfo@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves information about an installed or available code page (max char size, default char, lead bytes).

IsDBCSLeadByte@WIN32API.INC.desc: Determines whether a byte is a lead byte of a double-byte character in the system default ANSI code page.

CompareString@WIN32API.INC.desc: Compares two strings for a locale using flags such as case-insensitive. Returns CSTR_LESS_THAN, CSTR_EQUAL, CSTR_GREATER_THAN, or 0 on error.

LCMapString@WIN32API.INC.desc: Maps one string to another for a locale, e.g. upper/lower case conversion or generating a sort key.

GetTimeFormat@WIN32API.INC.desc: Formats a time as a time string for a specified locale. Returns the number of characters written, or 0 on failure.

SetThreadLocale@WIN32API.INC.desc: Sets the current locale of the calling thread.

GetStringTypeA@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves character type information (e.g. upper, digit, space) for each character in a string for a specified locale. Deprecated.

FoldString@WIN32API.INC.desc: Maps one string to another, performing a transformation such as converting full-width or precomposed characters.

EnumTimeFormats@WIN32API.INC.desc: Enumerates the time formats available for a specified locale via a callback function.

EnumDateFormats@WIN32API.INC.desc: Enumerates the long or short date formats available for a specified locale via a callback function.

IsValidLocale@WIN32API.INC.desc: Determines whether a locale identifier is installed or supported. Returns nonzero if valid.

ConvertDefaultLocale@WIN32API.INC.desc: Converts a default locale value (such as LOCALE_USER_DEFAULT) to an actual locale identifier.

EnumSystemLocales@WIN32API.INC.desc: Enumerates the locales installed or supported by the operating system via a callback function.

EnumSystemCodePages@WIN32API.INC.desc: Enumerates the code pages installed or supported by the operating system via a callback function.

ReadConsoleOutput@WIN32API.INC.desc: Reads character and color attribute data from a rectangular block of cells in a console screen buffer.

WriteConsoleOutput@WIN32API.INC.desc: Writes character and color attribute data to a rectangular block of cells in a console screen buffer.

ReadConsoleOutputCharacter@WIN32API.INC.desc: Copies characters from consecutive cells of a console screen buffer, starting at a specified location.

ReadConsoleOutputAttribute@WIN32API.INC.desc: Copies character attributes from consecutive cells of a console screen buffer, starting at a specified location.

WriteConsoleOutputCharacter@WIN32API.INC.desc: Copies characters to consecutive cells of a console screen buffer, starting at a specified location.

WriteConsoleOutputAttribute@WIN32API.INC.desc: Copies character attributes to consecutive cells of a console screen buffer, starting at a specified location.

FillConsoleOutputCharacter@WIN32API.INC.desc: Writes a character to the console screen buffer a specified number of times, starting at given coordinates.

FillConsoleOutputAttribute@WIN32API.INC.desc: Sets character attributes for a number of consecutive cells of a console screen buffer, starting at given coordinates.

GetConsoleMode@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves the current input mode of a console input buffer or the output mode of a console screen buffer.
